descriptionChirho: The Greek name Ἰάκωβος (from Hebrew יַעֲקֹב), borne by several persons in the NT: (1) James son of Zebedee, one of the Twelve, brother of John (Matt 4:21, 10:2, 17:1; Mark 1:19,29, 3:17, 5:37, 9:2, 10:35,41, 13:3; Acts 1:13, 12:2); (2) James son of Alphaeus, another of the Twelve (Matt 10:3; Mark 3:18; Luke 6:15; Acts 1:13); (3) James the brother of the Lord, leader of the Jerusalem church (Acts 12:17, 15:13, 21:18; 1 Cor 15:7; Gal 1:19, 2:9,12; author of the Epistle of James); (4) James the Less, son of Mary (Matt 27:56; Mark 15:40, 16:1; Luke 24:10); (5) James father of the apostle Judas (Luke 6:16; Acts 1:13; Jude 1:1). All inflectional forms (NMS, AMS, GMS, DMS) map to this single proper noun. Rendered Arabic يعقوب, French Jacques, German Jakobus, Korean 야고보, Spanish Iakobos/Santiago.
